$comment: Layer 05/06 delta L0506-D001 (TOOL-041): the prepared runtime numeric domain. Scenarios live in conformance/agent/prepared-runtime/, discriminated by a top-level `prepared_runtime` key. For each case a runner makes ONE tool call through the REAL Layer 06 pipeline (resolve, prepare_arguments, validation, the tools/pre-execute hook, execute) with a pre-execute listener that records the prepared value at each `observe` JSON pointer, and (custom tools) an execute that records the same. It performs no preparation, validation or numeric conversion itself. VALUE TOKENS (`token`): "+Infinity", "-Infinity", "NaN", "-0" (negative zero), or a finite JSON number literal; a finite literal MUST denote a finite binary64 value (a literal that overflows is not a finite token -- write "+Infinity"/"-Infinity"). An OBSERVED token is the ECMAScript Number::toString of the value (an integral value decoded as a binding integer renders the same way, e.g. "9007199254740992"). PREFLIGHT (language-neutral, before running a case; a violation fails the document, it is never defaulted): for outcome `prepared`, the keys of `observed` are exactly the `observe` pointers; every finite literal in `prepare_set` or `observed` parses to a finite binary64 value.

editCase.$comment: the REAL built-in edit tool over a fresh root holding f.txt = "a\n" (its own prepare_arguments, prepareEditArguments)

customCase.$comment: a tool named `probe` whose parameters are `schema` and whose prepare_arguments returns the arguments with `prepare_set` applied (Pi's public AgentTool.prepareArguments shim); its execute records the observed values and succeeds

schema.$comment: number: {type: object, properties: {limit: {type: number}}, required: [limit]}; integer: the same with {type: integer}; open: {type: object, properties: {}}

failure.$comment: Layer 06's certified immediate argument-validation error (TOOL-003; its text is Layer 06's own, not asserted); neither the hook nor execute runs
